q-5158.name: Question 1
q-5158.worked_solution:
The difference of squares formula is given by

$$
{a}^{2}-{b}^{2}=(a+b)(a-b)
$$

Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $2.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $2,$ as follows:

$$
162{x}^{4}-2=2\cdot 81{x}^{4}-2\cdot 1=2(81{x}^{4}-1)
$$

The expression in parentheses can be written as a difference of squares:

$$
2(81{x}^{4}-1)=2({(9{x}^{2})}^{2}-{1}^{2})
$$

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula:

$$
2({(9{x}^{2})}^{2}-{1}^{2})=2(9{x}^{2}+1)(9{x}^{2}-1)
$$

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(9{x}^{2}+1)(9{x}^{2}-1) & =2(9{x}^{2}+1)({(3x)}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =2(9{x}^{2}+1)(3x+1)(3x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

q-5158.html:
Question 1
?

Factor 162x4−2.

a
2(9x2+1)(x+3)(x−3)
b
2(9x2+1)(x+1)(x−1)
c
(9x2+1)(3x+1)(3x−1)
d
9(x2+1)(2x+1)(2x−1)
e
2(9x2+1)(3x+1)(3x−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The difference of squares formula is given by

a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b)

Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of 2. To simplify the computation, we can factor out the 2, as follows:

162x4−2=2⋅81x4−2⋅1=2(81x4−1)

The expression in parentheses can be written as a difference of squares: 2(81x4−1)=2((9x2)2−12)

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula: 2((9x2)2−12)=2(9x2+1)(9x2−1) Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows: 2(9x2+1)(9x2−1)=2(9x2+1)((3x)2−12)=2(9x2+1)(3x+1)(3x−1)

q-14136.name: Question 2
q-14136.worked_solution:
The difference of squares formula is given by

$$
{a}^{2}-{b}^{2}=(a+b)(a-b)
$$

Notice that all of the terms in our expression have a common factor of $5.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $5,$ as follows:

$$
405-5{x}^{4}=5\cdot 81-5\cdot {x}^{4}=5(81-{x}^{4})
$$

The expression in parentheses can be written as a difference of squares:

$$
5(81-{x}^{4})=5({9}^{2}-{({x}^{2})}^{2})
$$

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula:

$$
5({9}^{2}-{({x}^{2})}^{2})=5(9+{x}^{2})(9-{x}^{2})
$$

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5(9+{x}^{2})(9-{x}^{2}) & =5(9+{x}^{2})({3}^{2}-{x}^{2}) \\  & =5(9+{x}^{2})(3+x)(3-x)\end{aligned}
$$

q-14136.html:
Question 2
?

Factor 405−5x4 completely.

a
5(9+x2)(3−x)
b
5(9+x)(3+x)(3−x)
c
5(9+x2)(3+x)(3−x)
d
(9+x2)(3+x)(3−x)
e
(3+5x2)(3−5x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The difference of squares formula is given by

a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b)

Notice that all of the terms in our expression have a common factor of 5. To simplify the computation, we can factor out the 5, as follows:

405−5x4=5⋅81−5⋅x4=5(81−x4)

The expression in parentheses can be written as a difference of squares: 5(81−x4)=5(92−(x2)2)

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula: 5(92−(x2)2)=5(9+x2)(9−x2)

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows: 5(9+x2)(9−x2)=5(9+x2)(32−x2)=5(9+x2)(3+x)(3−x)

q-37704.name: Question 3
q-37704.worked_solution:
The difference of squares formula is given by

$$
{a}^{2}-{b}^{2}=(a+b)(a-b)
$$

Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $q.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the $q,$ as follows:

$$
q-q{p}^{4}=q(1-{p}^{4})
$$

The expression in parenthesis can be written as a difference of squares:

$$
q(1-{p}^{4})=q({1}^{2}-{({p}^{2})}^{2})
$$

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula:

$$
q({1}^{2}-{({p}^{2})}^{2})=q(1+{p}^{2})(1-{p}^{2})
$$

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1+{p}^{2})(1-{p}^{2}) & =q(1+{p}^{2})({1}^{2}-{p}^{2}) \\  & =q(1+{p}^{2})(1+p)(1-p)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Factor the expression q−qp4.

a
(1+p2)(q+p)(q−p)
b
q(1+p2)(1+p)2
c
q(1+p2)(1−p)2
d
q(1+p2)(1+p)(1−p)
e
(q+p2)(1+p)(1−p)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The difference of squares formula is given by

a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b)

Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of q. To simplify the computation, we can factor out the q, as follows:

q−qp4=q(1−p4)

The expression in parenthesis can be written as a difference of squares: q(1−p4)=q(12−(p2)2)

Now, we factor our expression using the difference of squares formula: q(12−(p2)2)=q(1+p2)(1−p2)

Finally, we notice that the expression in the second set of parentheses is also a difference of squares. Therefore, the expression can be factored further, as follows: q(1+p2)(1−p2)=q(1+p2)(12−p2)=q(1+p2)(1+p)(1−p)
